description: A color's invoiced amount is the number of invoice line items for products of that color.

d.request: For each product color (treating NULL colors as a separate group), count the number of invoice line items; calculate each color's share of total invoice line items; filter to colors whose item count exceeds the average item count per color; and report one row with these above-average colors' average invoiced item count, average share of total, and average excess above the per-color mean.
d.sql:
WITH color_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    p.product_color,
    COUNT(*) as item_count
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY p.product_color
),
total_items AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) as total FROM Invoice_Line_Items
),
avg_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(item_count) as avg_item_count FROM color_counts
),
color_with_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    cc.item_count,
    cc.item_count / (SELECT total FROM total_items) as share,
    cc.item_count - (SELECT avg_item_count FROM avg_count) as excess
  FROM color_counts cc
  WHERE cc.item_count > (SELECT avg_item_count FROM avg_count)
)
SELECT 
  AVG(item_count) as avg_invoiced_item_count,
  AVG(share) as avg_share_of_total,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess_above_per_color_mean
FROM color_with_stats

a.request: For each product color, count how many invoice line items were for products of that color. Products with no color count as their own group. Work out each color's share of the overall number of line items. Keep the colors whose count is above the average count per color. Over those colors, give one row with the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the count exceeds the per-color average. Don't round anything.
a.sql:
WITH color_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    p.product_color,
    COUNT(*) as color_count
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY p.product_color
),
stats AS (
  SELECT 
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice_Line_Items) as total_items,
    AVG(color_count) as avg_count_per_color
  FROM color_counts
),
filtered_colors AS (
  SELECT 
    cc.color_count,
    cc.color_count * 1.0 / s.total_items as share,
    cc.color_count - s.avg_count_per_color as exceeds_average
  FROM color_counts cc
  CROSS JOIN stats s
  WHERE cc.color_count > s.avg_count_per_color
)
SELECT 
  AVG(color_count) as avg_count,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(exceeds_average) as avg_exceeds
FROM filtered_colors

c.request: How much of each product color was invoiced? Products with no color count as their own group. Work out each color's share of the total invoiced. Look at the colors whose invoiced amount is above the average per color. For those colors, give one row with their average invoiced amount, their average share, and how far above the per-color average they are on average. Don't round anything. A color's invoiced amount is the number of invoice line items for products of that color.
c.sql:
WITH color_invoices AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(p.product_color, 'No Color') as color,
    COUNT(*) as invoiced_amount
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY COALESCE(p.product_color, 'No Color')
),
stats AS (
  SELECT 
    invoiced_amount,
    invoiced_amount / (SELECT SUM(invoiced_amount) FROM color_invoices) as share,
    (SELECT AVG(invoiced_amount) FROM color_invoices) as avg_inv
  FROM color_invoices
)
SELECT 
  AVG(invoiced_amount) as avg_invoiced_amount,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(invoiced_amount - avg_inv) as avg_above_average
FROM stats
WHERE invoiced_amount > avg_inv

b.request: Count invoice line items per product color (with NULL as a separate group), compute each color's share of total line item count, identify colors exceeding the average line item count, and output one row with their average count, average share, and average excess above the per-color average.
b.sql:
WITH color_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    p.product_color,
    COUNT(*) as line_item_count
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Products p ON ili.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY p.product_color
),
with_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    cc.product_color,
    cc.line_item_count,
    SUM(cc.line_item_count) OVER () as total_count,
    AVG(cc.line_item_count) OVER () as avg_count
  FROM color_counts cc
),
enriched AS (
  SELECT 
    product_color,
    line_item_count,
    line_item_count / total_count as color_share,
    avg_count,
    line_item_count - avg_count as excess
  FROM with_totals
  WHERE line_item_count > avg_count
)
SELECT 
  AVG(line_item_count) as average_count,
  AVG(color_share) as average_share,
  AVG(excess) as average_excess
FROM enriched;
